subject: Post-call recap: log redaction checklist & residency preferences
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finexa-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: log redaction checklist & residency preferences

Hi Alice — thanks again for joining the call earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

What we heard from Finexa (priorities):
- EU data residency for request/response logs and any persistent artifacts.
- Strict redaction of PII in both request and response logs (names, emails, payment tokens).
- Headers and trace IDs: prefer masking at ingest, but retain non-identifying trace metadata for perf debugging.
- Retention target: 90 days for operational logs, 365 days for audit logs (encrypted).
- Need SOC2 artifacts and an evidence extract for a procurement review.

Open items / asks we committed to:
1) Share a lightweight log-redaction checklist (how masking/redaction works end-to-end) — attachment: log-redaction-checklist.xlsx
2) Confirm exact residency options and where we store raw vs. redacted logs (EU regions only for Finexa)
3) Provide a sample of the SOC2 evidence extract and retention policy doc (we'll scope what subset Finexa needs)
4) Propose a short pilot: 2-week ingest of synthetic traffic into a sandbox with our masking layer enabled so Finexa can validate redaction

Can you confirm the residency requirement is strictly EU-only (no backup outside EU) and whether the 90/365 split matches your expectations? Once we get that, I’ll coordinate with Marissa and Security to pull the SOC2 extract and the network diagram.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: log-redaction-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 12 KB)
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finexa-pay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@finexa-pay.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: log redaction checklist & residency preferences

Thanks Karthik — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: EU-only is a hard requirement for both raw and processed logs. No replication or backups outside the EU without explicit, written consent from our InfoSec.
- Trace IDs / headers: We want trace IDs pseudonymized (consistent hash mapping per request but unlinkable to a user id). Full request IDs are fine for short-term debugging but should be redacted or rotated before longer retention buckets.
- Retention: 90 days for request/response logs is fine for the initial pilot. Audit logs (access, config changes) need to be retained 365 days as encrypted extracts.
- SOC2: we need the sections that cover logging, access controls, and key management (particularly KMS rotation records). If you can provide an extracted bundle and a short mapping doc that shows where each control lives in Redwood’s environment, that would speed procurement.

Pilot ask: Can you stand up a sandbox in eu-west-1 (or frankfurt) with masking enabled? We will feed a subset of synthetic transactions and validate that emails and payment tokens are removed from stored logs. Timeline: target pilot start week of Aug 31.

If Security needs a call to dig into trace pseudonymization, loop them in — happy to arrange.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Head of Platform Security, Finexa Payments

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Alice's response. Action items for internal owners:

- Ben: please pull the SOC2 extract focused on logging, access controls, and KMS rotation logs. We should redact any customer-identifying data before sharing. Attachment request: SOC2-extract-request.pdf (template we send to Compliance).
- Ben / Security: confirm we can commit to EU-only residency (including backups). If there are any edge cases (e.g., cross-region replication for HA), flag them now.
- Karthik: can you validate the pilot scope and confirm availability to set up an eu-west sandbox (frankfurt preferred)? We will need an infra ticket and a small runbook for Finexa to run their synthetic feed.

Internal note: keep the external thread polite and concise. If Security needs to join the thread to provide technical detail on pseudonymization, do so but include a single point of contact.

Thanks — I’ll help coordinate timelines with Prod Infra.

Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-extract-request.pdf (pdf, 28 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finexa-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: log redaction checklist & residency preferences

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick clarifications. Confirming next steps and proposed timeline below:

1) Residency: Confirmed — we will provision the sandbox and any persistent storage in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). No backups will be stored outside EU unless Finexa signs an exception.
2) Pilot: We will stand up the sandbox the week of Aug 31. Karthik + infra will share runbook and synthetic-data template by Aug 26.
3) Trace IDs: We will enable deterministic pseudonymization (HMAC with a per-tenant salt stored in KMS) for the pilot so Finexa can validate unlinkability. Short-lived full request IDs will be available only in ephemeral debugging sessions and will not be persisted to the 90-day bucket.
4) SOC2 evidence: Ben will ship the SOC2 extract bundle and a mapping doc by Aug 25. We will scrub any unrelated customer identifiers before delivery.

Attachments: log-redaction-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram.png
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FINEXA-2026-08-01

If that timeline works, I’ll open the infra ticket and schedule a 30-min kickoff with Finexa Security for Aug 26 to walk through pseudonymization details.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
